assessingAuthority.value: Trades Recognition Australia (TRA), within the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
assessingAuthority.quote: Trades Recognition Australia (TRA) is a skills assessment service for people with trade skills gained overseas or in Australia for the purpose of migration.

occupationsAssessedByTRA.value: All 9 occupations appear on TRA's 'Australian Qualifications by Occupation' list (current from 3 December 2025)

tradeGroupSplit.value: TRA defines exactly four 'Licensed Occupations': 342111 Airconditioning and Refrigeration Mechanic, 341111 Electrician (General), 341112 Electrician (Special Class), 334111 Plumber (General). The other five in this group (341113, 334112, 334113, 334114, 334115) are not TRA 'licensed occupations' and follow the standard international-graduate pathway.
tradeGroupSplit.quote: Licensed Occupation – This refers to the occupations of Airconditioning and Refrigeration Mechanic, Electrician (General), Electrician (Special Class) and Plumber (General).

value.purpose: for recent international graduates applying for Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485, Post-Vocational Education Work Stream); prerequisite for the Job Ready Program
eligibility: Australian qualification completed through a CRICOS-registered RTO

provisionalSkillsAssessment.quote: The Provisional Skills Assessment Program is for recent international graduates who wish to apply for a Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) also known as the Post-Vocational Education Work Stream.

value.status: open (TRA program page live; guidelines last updated April 2026, v37.0; JRP news items dated July 2026)
value.appliesTo: non-licensed TRA occupations only (in this group: 341113, 334112, 334113, 334114, 334115)
value.prerequisite: successful PSA within the last 3 years
steps: Job Ready Workplace Assessment (JRWA) by TRA-approved RTO assessor at the workplace, after 6 months full-time-equivalent paid employment and TRA invitation – $2,845
value.employment: minimum 12 months full-time (avg 38 h/week; part-time pro-rata) paid employment in Australia with TRA-approved employer(s), completed within 3 years; at least 6 months FTE with one employer; max 5 employers; up to 3 months prior employment may be claimed
value.outcome: skills assessment outcome letter usable for a skilled visa

jobReadyProgram.quote: The Job Ready Program is a minimum 12-month employment-based skills assessment that verifies your applied skills meet the Australian standards in your Nominated Occupation.

jobReadyProgramLicensedExclusion.quote: The following licensed occupations are not eligible for the Job Ready Program

jobReadyProgramAudience.value: international student graduates of an Australian VET course working in Australia
jobReadyProgramAudience.quote: This program is for international student graduates of an Australian Vocational Education and Training (VET) course, who are working in Australia and seeking a pathway to a skilled visa.

value.appliesTo: compulsory for permanent migration in the four TRA licensed occupations (all countries), except 482 (ask Home Affairs) and 485 (use PSA)
value.pathway2: for applicants who have a relevant Australian VET qualification or a current identified Australian occupation licence (without restrictions) – i.e. the route for an Australian-trained graduate in a licensed trade
value.pathway2Steps: documentary evidence (incl. Australian VET qualification/licence and employment evidence) + technical interview, via a TRA-approved RTO
value.pathway1Experience: licensed trade: 4 years with formal training / 6 years without
value.processing: approx. 15 weeks after complete documentary evidence (as of July 2026)
value.registrationPause: OSAP/TSS registrations paused 14–29 March 2026, recommenced 30 March 2026 (refreshed RTO panel)

offshoreSkillsAssessmentProgram.quote: Pathway 2 is for applicants who have a relevant Australian VET qualification or a current identified Australian occupation licence (without restrictions).

osapCompulsoryLicensed.value: OSAP compulsory for permanent migration in the four licensed occupations
osapCompulsoryLicensed.quote: This program is compulsory if you are applying for permanent migration in the following licensed occupations

osapLicensed485Exception.value: For the licensed occupations, 485 applicants use the PSA instead of OSAP; 482 applicants must seek Home Affairs advice
osapLicensed485Exception.quote: Applicants from all countries in this occupation are required to have an OSAP assessment unless you are applying for a: 482 visa

otsr.value: Offshore Technical Skills Record (OTSR) is issued for licensed occupations under OSAP Pathway 1 (overseas-trained); used to apply for a provisional/restricted licence, then Australian-context gap training + supervised employment to obtain the Australian VET qualification. The guidelines describe Pathway 2 (Australian VET qualification) as producing an outcome letter only.
otsr.quote: If you nominated a TRA-licensed occupation, you will be issued an Offshore Technical Skills Record.

migrationSkillsAssessment.quote: This program is a pathway for people applying for a skilled migration visa in occupations and countries that are not required to be assessed in any of our other programs.

traDoesNotLicense.value: TRA does not issue licences; applicants must separately meet state/territory licensing requirements
traDoesNotLicense.quote: We do not award Australian qualifications, occupational registrations or occupational licences.

constructionPrioritisation.value: TRA prioritised assessments for targeted construction occupations 1 July 2024 – 30 June 2026 (no fee); no official extension beyond 30 June 2026 found
constructionPrioritisation.quote: Between 1 July 2024 and 30 June 2026 Trades Recognition Australia (TRA) will be  prioritising skills assessments for  targeted construction occupations

australianStudyRoute.value: See per-occupation qualification from TRA's 'Australian Qualifications by Occupation' (current from 3 Dec 2025). TRA may accept alternative/older versions if relevant. Nominal durations: not stated in any official source checked.
australianStudyRoute.quote: Where a TRA skills assessment requires an Australian qualification alternative qualifications or older versions of the qualification may be accepted if they are relevant to your occupation

general.value: Occupational licensing is the responsibility of state/territory licensing authorities
general.quote: occupational licensing is the responsibility of the relevant state or territory licensing authority.

visaMaintenance.value: Applicant must keep a valid visa throughout the JRP; TRA gives no visa advice
visaMaintenance.quote: It is your responsibility to make sure that you maintain a visa for the duration of your time in the program.

jrpEmploymentInAustraliaOnly.value: All JRP employment must be in Australia
jrpEmploymentInAustraliaOnly.quote: No. All employment under the JRP must be undertaken within Australia.

gaps: QLD electrical licence (Electrical Safety Office / WorkSafe QLD) set to null: worksafe.qld.gov.au and its Electrical Licensing Eligibility Guide PDF returned HTTP 403 (bot protection) so could not be read directly. Search-index snippets indicate the RTO sends a completion statement (ATF-012) to the ESO after the apprenticeship (UEE30820, Capstone via Skills Assure Supplier) – verify manually before using.

VIC plumbing (Building and Plumbing Commission, formerly VBA) set to null for all plumbing occupations: bpc.vic.gov.au and vba.vic.gov.au returned HTTP 403. Search snippets suggest registration requires Cert III via apprenticeship + prescribed units + BPC registration exam, and licence needs extra experience + licence exam – unverified.
QLD licensing for mechanical services plumbing, gasfitting and roof plumbing not checked (gas work in QLD may be regulated by a different body than QBCC) – null.
Lift Mechanic (341113) registration: no official state licensing page found/checked – null.
Electrician (Special Class) (341112): no official source found distinguishing it from 341111 for assessment/licensing beyond the same Cert III (UEE30820) – specialClassNote null.
AC&R Mechanic (342111) state electrical (restricted) licence requirements not checked – null.

OSAP Pathway 2 minimum years of employment is not stated in the OSAP guidelines (April 2026) or evidence factsheet (Pathway 1 is 4 yrs with formal training for licensed trades). Also the guidelines say Pathway 2 = technical interview + employer evidence, while the evidence factsheet says the technical assessment includes 'a Practical Assessment for licenced occupations' – unresolved inconsistency.
Whether OSAP Pathway 2 for a licensed trade issues an OTSR or a full outcome only: guidelines mention OTSR only under Pathway 1.

Whether an Australian-trained graduate in a non-licensed occupation (334112–334115, 341113) may use the Migration Skills Assessment instead of the JRP is not explicitly stated; MSA page only excludes 485/482 applicants and licensed occupations.
No nominal course durations stated in official sources checked (VIC ESV refers to a 4-year apprenticeship contract for electricians only).
No Home Affairs page was successfully retrieved (skilled occupation list is JS-rendered); list status (MLTSSL/CSOL) and visa-specific skills assessment requirements not confirmed here.
Construction prioritisation (1 Jul 2024–30 Jun 2026) appears in the JRP FAQ; no official statement found about extension past 30 June 2026.
QBCC occupational plumber page still cites CPC32413 (superseded) whereas TRA lists CPC32420; reported as-is.
